The Kazan Icon of the Mother of God

Icons

Theotokos

The Kazan Icon of the Mother of God

Our Lady of Kazan · Kazanskaya

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Luke 1:41–45

King James Version · Scripture previews

The Kazan icon is especially venerated in the Russian Church, with important examples associated with Kazan, Saint Petersburg and Moscow. The OCA’s July 8 account relates its discovery and the subsequent veneration of multiple copies.

[1] Opening paragraphs; account of the first copy

What is depicted

The pictured panel is a mid-nineteenth-century Kazan icon, with smaller saints on the borders. Mary inclines her head beside the upright Christ child. This later example is identified separately from the icon whose discovery is narrated for 1579.

[2] Displayed work; file-page title and description

History and tradition

The published Church account places the discovery after a destructive fire in Kazan in 1579. Nine-year-old Matrona reported repeated visions indicating the location. The account names the priest Ermogenes, later patriarch, as a witness who wrote about the finding.

[1] 1579 fire; Matrona; priest Ermogenes

Published explanation

The OCA relates healings of blind people during the icon’s first procession and explains the prominence of its veneration. These reported miracles belong to the source’s Church narrative. The many later copies should not all be called the same original physical object.

[1] First healings; detailed report and exact copy

And it came to pass, that, when Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the babe leaped in her womb; and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Ghost: And she spake out with a loud voice, and said, Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb. And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?

[3] Luke 1:41–43
